title: An intersection of quasi-compact opens in an ind-quasi-affine scheme identifies with an intersection of quasi-compact opens in an affine scheme, and opens of X inside E map to opens of Y

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-sits-in-functions (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 3210-3224

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: The ringed space (E, O_X|_E) is locally ringed, so the morphism-into-affine lemma applies to the identity A = Gamma(E, O_X|_E) and produces the canonical morphism j into Spec(A). Write E as the intersection of a nonempty directed family of quasi-compact opens U_i of X and set A_i = Gamma(U_i, O_{U_i}). For each i there is a commutative square from (E, O_X|_E) and (U_i, O_{U_i}) into Spec(A) and Spec(A_i). Since U_i is quasi-affine, U_i to Spec(A_i) is a quasi-compact open immersion; since A = colim A_i, Spec(A) = lim Spec(A_i) as topological spaces (limits-lemma-topology-limit); and E = lim U_i (topology-lemma-make-spectral-space). Hence E to Spec(A) is a homeomorphism onto its image E', and E' is the intersection of the inverse images of the opens U_i of Spec(A_i); moreover for every e in E the local ring O_{X, e} equals the value of O_{U_i, e}, which agrees with the value on Spec(A). For the final assertion pick i, j with U_i inside U_j and consider the three commutative squares for U_i and W over Spec(A_i) and Spec(A_j) and over Spec(A). By properties-lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine the first square is cartesian, hence so is the second, and passing to the limit the third is cartesian, so the top horizontal arrow W to Spec(A) is an open immersion; that is, j(W) is open in Y. (source lines 3226-3278)

core_obligations: Set up: (E, O_X|_E) is a locally ringed space, so schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine applies to A = Gamma(E, O_X|_E) and yields the canonical morphism j into Y = Spec(A) (proof lines 3227-3229). Write E = intersection of U_i, i in a nonempty index set, directed so that for i, j there is k with U_k inside U_i intersect U_j, and put A_i = Gamma(U_i, O_{U_i}); form the commutative squares from E and U_i into Spec(A) and Spec(A_i) (proof lines 3229-3241). Since U_i is quasi-affine, U_i to Spec(A_i) is a quasi-compact open immersion; A = colim A_i gives Spec(A) = lim Spec(A_i) topologically by limits-lemma-topology-limit; E = lim U_i by topology-lemma-make-spectral-space; hence E to Spec(A) is a homeomorphism onto its image E', and E' is the intersection of the inverse images of the opens U_i of Spec(A_i); for every e in E the local ring O_{X, e} is the value of O_{U_i, e}, the same as the value on Spec(A), giving the isomorphism onto (E', O_Y|_{E'}) with E' an intersection of quasi-compact opens (proof lines 3242-3251). Final assertion: pick i, j with U_i inside U_j; the three commutative squares for U_i and W over Spec(A_i), Spec(A_j) and Spec(A) are considered; properties-lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine makes the first cartesian, hence the second, and the limit of the second family is cartesian, so the top horizontal arrow W to Spec(A) is an open immersion, i.e. j(W) is open in Y (proof lines 3254-3277).
proof_roadmap: Produce the canonical morphism j via the morphism-into-affine lemma applied to the locally ringed space (E, O_X|_E) (proof lines 3227-3229).
Direct the family of quasi-compact opens and identify Spec(A) as the limit of the Spec(A_i) while E is the limit of the U_i (proof lines 3229-3247).
Conclude the homeomorphism onto E', the description of E' as an intersection of inverse images of quasi-compact opens, and the equality of local rings at every point of E (proof lines 3247-3251).
Prove the final assertion by the three-square cartesian argument over Spec(A_i), Spec(A_j) and the limit Spec(A) (proof lines 3254-3277).
